messages:
Priya Shah: Heads up — we're getting a spike in p99 latency for EU requests since ~09:12 UTC. Multiple customer escalations saying calls hang around TLS handshake and then timeout. I can see a surge in TLS retries in the logs.

network-bot: Alert: eu-west-1 ingress TLS handshake latency > 600ms (p99) for last 5m. 4xx/5xx rate unchanged.

Ben Ortega: Seen similar flagged by synthetic monitors. Mostly 10-20% of requests that hit 'ingress-proxy-euw-02' show 0.6-1.2s handshakes, then occasional connection resets.

Maya Chen: Anything changed on the edge route or BGP? I didn't push changes in last 24h.

Ajay Patel: No infra deploys. We did a vendor AS path change (cloud-net) for capacity at 08:50 UTC — might correlate. Opening a ticket with provider now.

Priya Shah: Repro steps from customer: curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:52.17.11.22 https://api.redwood.ai/ -v --tlsv1.3 --connect-timeout 5
Priya Shah: Timing shows TLS handshake takes 700-900ms then request either completes or drops.

Maya Chen: Can someone run a traceroute/tcpdump on the proxy host hitting that client IP? I want to see cross-AZ hops and retransmits.

Ben Ortega: Running traceroute from proxy:

```
$ traceroute -n 52.17.11.22
 1  10.0.1.1  0.5 ms  0.6 ms  0.5 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  1.2 ms  0.9 ms  1.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.45  8.7 ms  9.1 ms  9.0 ms
 4  203.0.113.12  150.2 ms  148.9 ms  149.6 ms
 5  52.17.11.22  150.9 ms  149.7 ms  151.3 ms
```

Ben Ortega: That ~150ms jump between hop 3 and 4 looks like cross-region/peering detour.

Ajay Patel: tcpdump during handshake shows visible RTT increases and several TLS retransmissions: `TLSv1.3 ClientHello` then gap ~120-200ms before `ServerHello`.

Priya Shah: DNS lookups — some clients resolving to eu-west edge but traffic being routed via partner-poP in another region. Could be a geo-DNS or peering issue.

Maya Chen: Can we confirm EDNS/geo records?

Priya Shah: Dig for api.redwood.ai from affected client: `dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` -> `52.17.11.22` (eu-west pool). From inside our VPC, the resolution is same IP, but the network path goes out to partner and comes back.

Ajay Patel: Provider responded: we had a transient route flap between our EU peer and their backbone; traffic got re-homed to an alternate POP in eu-central which increased MPLS transit and added 120-160ms. They say routes are stable now but BGP flap could explain p99.

Maya Chen: Mitigation options: 1) force fallback to a different eu-west PoP via smart routing for a rolling window 2) push route prep to avoid that vendor path 3) raise TCP/TLS timeout for affected customers (ugly).

Ben Ortega: Short-term: can we add a routing policy to prefer direct cloud-provider peering (avoid partner PoP) for 5m while provider finishes converge? That should reduce handshake RTT.

Priya Shah: I'm going to create a canary route policy to bias queries to eu-west-1a PoP and add a header-check to confirm which PoP serves the request. Will roll to 5% then ramp.

Maya Chen: Also enable TLS session resumption caching (if not already) to reduce handshake work for repeated connections. Ajay, is session ticket working across our proxies currently?

Ajay Patel: We already have session tickets, but if clients are routed through different PoPs they won't hit the same cache. Sticky routing or longer session ticket lifetime will help. I'll increase session ticket lifetime by 30m for the canary.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0415-01 — EU ingress TLS latency spike. Severity: P2. Owner: Maya Chen.

Priya Shah: Canary policy applied to 5% at 09:46 UTC. Monitoring p99 and error rate.

Ben Ortega: Early signal: canary shows p99 drop from 900ms -> 120ms for routed users, error rate down for that cohort. Good sign.

Maya Chen: Vendor reported route fully converged at 10:05 UTC. We're seeing overall p99 trending down, but some residual retries for long-lived clients.

Ajay Patel: Rolling config: 1) keep canary for 15m, 2) increase session ticket lifetime, 3) add a transient retry policy at ingress to do one fast-second-try on alternate PoP when handshake exceeds 300ms. Implementing now.

Priya Shah: Adding customer-facing notes to support thread: explain transient network reroute causing longer TLS handshakes and that we've mitigated via routing bias and session caching tweaks.

Ben Ortega: Postmortem checklist: collect tcpdump + traceroute from affected proxies, vendor BGP logs, DNS resolution snapshots, and timeline of canary changes.

Maya Chen: Follow-ups: 1) Ask provider for RCA and BGP community values to avoid future asymmetric re-homing. 2) Evaluate automatic short-circuiting in smart routing when handshake latency spikes. 3) Add synthetic test for TLS handshake p99 per PoP.

Priya Shah: Last observed p99 at 10:12 UTC is back to baseline ~95ms. Closing customer escalations. Will file full writeup in incidents/ and link to this thread. :white_check_mark:

Ajay Patel: Updating runbook with new retry policy snippet. Example ingress config we applied: 

```
routing_policy:
  prefer_pop: "eu-west-1a"
  weight: 0.05
ingress:
  tls_session_ticket_lifetime_seconds: 1800
  handshake_retry_threshold_ms: 300
  handshake_retry_action: "fast-failover-to-alt-pop"
```

Ben Ortega: Thanks all — solid quick mitigation. I'll tidy logs and attach to INC-2026-0415-01.

Priya Shah: Great. Closing thread.
